section_summary: This section centers on Japan’s January 23, 1949 general election: foreign press reactions, a detailed U.S. political mission analysis, and a contrasting report from occupation headquarters. It also covers the assassination of a Korean rightist leader in Tokyo, a proposed U.S. visit by economist Hyoye Ouchi, debate over occupation policy, and the formation of Yoshida’s new cabinet.

subfiles.title: Soviet press interpretation of the Japanese election
subfiles.about: Reports a Literary Gazette article presenting Communist gains as evidence of democratic progress in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The telegram describes Soviet praise for Communist gains and criticism of alleged repression.

subfiles.title: Izvestiya report on Japanese Communist united front proposal
subfiles.about: Reports a TASS account of the Japanese Communist Party’s proposed united front.
subfiles.summary: Izvestiya outlines a proposed alliance with Socialist and Labor-Farmer parties and its thirteen-point program.

subfiles.title: Chinese editorials on the Japanese election
subfiles.about: Summarizes Chinese newspaper warnings about conservatism, capitalism, communism, and renewed Japanese militarism.
subfiles.summary: Two editorials fear conservative rule and renewed militarism while emphasizing Communist electoral gains.

subfiles.title: Assassination of prominent Korean rightist leader in Japan
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits intelligence on the murder of Korean rightist leader Gen Ko Sho.
subfiles.summary: Sebald describes a suspected political killing, weak police progress, and its damaging effect on Korean rightists.

subfiles.title: Spot intelligence on assassination of Gen Ko Sho
subfiles.about: Reports the circumstances and possible repercussions of Gen Ko Sho’s shooting near Ueno Station.
subfiles.summary: The report identifies Gen as a Korean anti-communist leader and warns of possible violent reactions.

subfiles.title: Editorial on the development of Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a translation of a Kunming newspaper editorial entitled “Where is Japan Heading?”
subfiles.summary: The cover identifies the newspaper and its connection to provincial finance commissioner Lin Nan-yuan.

subfiles.title: Where is Japan Heading?
subfiles.about: Argues that U.S. support is enabling renewed Japanese militarism.
subfiles.summary: The editorial alleges that Japanese police, naval forces, airfields, industry, and conservative politics amount to rearmament. It portrays American economic policy as a route back to fascist militarism.

subfiles.title: James L. Fieser to Dean G. Acheson
subfiles.about: Describes Fieser’s Japan visit and his Christian university project.
subfiles.summary: Fieser recalls meetings with Japanese and occupation leaders, thanks the State Department for travel assistance, and sends related materials.

subfiles.title: Proposed visit to the United States of Hyoye Ouchi
subfiles.about: Explains why SCAP denied economist Hyoye Ouchi permission to visit the United States.
subfiles.summary: The mission favored Ouchi’s scholarly visit despite reports describing him as a fellow traveler. SCAP’s Chief of Staff refused permission.

subfiles.title: Request to reconsider Hyoye Ouchi’s travel
subfiles.to: Acting Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Asks that SCAP reconsider permission for Ouchi to travel to the United States.
subfiles.summary: The Department cites Ouchi’s official appointments and scholarly travel; it has no objection to a visitor visa.

subfiles.title: Japanese general election of January 23, 1949
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits and summarizes a detailed analysis of the Japanese general election.
subfiles.summary: Sebald reports a Democratic Liberal majority of 264 seats, Communist growth to 35 seats, and heavy losses for centrist parties. He attributes the result partly to Yoshida’s independence, weak coalition leadership, and effective Communist organization. He also assesses election administration and the challenges facing the new majority.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japanese general election of January 23, 1949
subfiles.from: Charles Nelson Spinks, Foreign Service Officer
subfiles.about: Analyzes turnout, votes, seats, regional patterns, and political causes of the 1949 election result.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum compares the 1947 and 1949 elections through extensive tables of seats, votes, candidates, occupations, ages, and prefectural results. It examines conservative and Communist gains, centrist losses, campaign strategy, and regional differences. It also notes the first popular review of Supreme Court justices.

subfiles.title: Views of Mr. Kades, Deputy Chief of Government Section
subfiles.about: Introduces Green’s notes on discussions with Charles Kades about Japanese politics and occupation policy.
subfiles.summary: Green says the election unsettled Kades and argues that occupation policy should better follow NSC 13/2.

subfiles.title: Notes on discussions with Charles Kades
subfiles.about: Records Kades’s assessments of election results, Yoshida, occupation interference, public service law, and police reform.
subfiles.summary: Kades expects further conservative strength and socialist weakness, and describes tensions between SCAP sections over intervention in Japanese government. Green adds comments questioning several of Kades’s views. The notes also address economic stabilization, the National Public Service Law, and centralized police powers.

subfiles.title: Formation of the new Yoshida cabinet
subfiles.about: Discusses the new Yoshida cabinet and negotiations with Democratic Party leader Ken Inukai.
subfiles.summary: The surviving text reports a cabinet committed to stabilization and anti-communism, with Inukai’s faction joining despite a threatened Democratic Party split.

subfiles.title: Harry F. Kern to W. Walton Butterworth
subfiles.about: Thanks Butterworth for speaking with the American Council on Japan.
subfiles.summary: Kern welcomes cooperation with the State Department and proposes another meeting in Washington.

subfiles.title: General Headquarters report on Japanese election of January 23, 1949
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards and critiques SCAP Government Section’s election report.
subfiles.summary: Sebald argues that the headquarters report understates Democratic Liberal and Communist gains and overlooks Yoshida’s appeal as an independent leader. He disputes its treatment of socialist defections while praising its account of election procedures and statistical material.

subfiles.title: Election report: transmittal memorandum
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Submits the headquarters report on the general election and Supreme Court referendum.
subfiles.summary: Whitney highlights the conservative victory, confirmation of the justices, and orderly representative government.

subfiles.title: General Elections of January 23, 1949: title and contents
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Introduces the report and lists its sections on the House election and judicial referendum.
subfiles.summary: The title page quotes MacArthur; the contents outline election administration, campaign coverage, statistics, and judicial review.
